title: A non-holder's `engram work note` from another checkout voids the holder's carried gate credit (attributed to the item's named root, not the real cwd)
outcome: A command run by a session that isn't the holder, from a working directory outside the holder's named root, never voids the holder's carried check. Commands are attributed by their real cwd, not by the item focus a tracker command moves.
acceptance: C1 (diagnosis). The item records, with source locators, why check 7921f177… refused test-b4eb5619 (and 332d1e4681be's occurrence): a Claude Bash subshell `cd` into the holder's root left the session's shell lost among places that include that root, and the session's later lines, though they began with their own absolute `cd` to another checkout, were placed at those lost places, so the other-session fence named the holder's root.

C2 (subshell). For a Claude session, whose Bash tool runs bash, a directory change inside a top-level `( … )` subshell does not move or lose the session's shell. The subshell's own commands are still placed where its `cd` leads, so a write there still fences a gate in that root. A `{ …; }` group, a pipeline element, `eval`, or a non-bash runtime keep today's conservative handling.

C3 (leading absolute cd). For a Claude session, a line that starts with `cd ABS &&` (a literal absolute directory that resolves; joined by `&&`, not `;` or `||`) places the rest of the line at ABS alone, not at the lost shell's places. A line whose first change is joined by `;`, or is relative or computed, keeps today's placement.

C4 (tests). Through the production command-start path: a session's `(cd <holder root> && <command>)` followed by `cd <other checkout> && engram work note <holder item> …` leaves the holder's carried gate credited; the same with no subshell (`cd <holder root> && <command that writes>`) still refuses it; a write inside the subshell while the gate is carried still refuses it; `cd <holder root>; cd <other> && x` and a relative leading cd keep today's behaviour; a non-Claude runtime is unchanged.

C5 (refusal text). When an other-session command refuses a gate, the cause also names where TermAl placed it: the line's leading absolute directory, or "a shell TermAl could not follow", instead of "there" alone.

C6 (validation and landing). The full gate passes on the exact tree submitted for landing; the review pair has no outstanding finding of Medium or higher; the item carries the evidence the standing landing rule requires.
